texts.li: [lowtech] A hunting party of {FACTION} has followed a herd onto the colony's land. Their leader, {X_nameDef}, told {A_nameDef} they mean to camp {PLACE} until the herd moves on, and to take what game they need while it's here.

[!lowtech] A hunting party of {FACTION} has tracked game onto the colony's land, rifles slung and packs heavy. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} they'll set up camp {PLACE} and stay until the hunting thins out.
Hunters of {FACTION} came through the trees this morning and stopped to look the land over. {X_nameDef} says the game here is too good to pass up. They are heading for a spot {PLACE} to make camp.

settled.li: The hunters from {FACTION} finished their camp {PLACE}: bedrolls around a fire, and a spot for dressing game.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef} from the hunters' camp has spent more evenings at the colony than at the camp fire lately. The colony feeds people better than the trail does, {X_pronoun} says, and {X_nameDef} would like to stay.

farewell.li: The herd moved on, and the hunters from {FACTION} went with it. Their camp {PLACE} is packed up and gone, and the land is quieter.
The hunters from {FACTION} packed up their camp {PLACE} and moved on after the game, as hunters do.

lines.li: Whose turn is it to skin?

texts.li: A family of {FACTION} has come down the road with everything they own on their backs. Their home is gone, burned or taken, and {X_nameDef} would rather not say which. They ask only for a patch of ground {PLACE} to rest on for a while.

[lowtech] Refugees of {FACTION}, a family by the look of them, have stopped near the colony with a cart and a few bundles. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef}, politely, whether anyone would mind if they camped {PLACE} for a time.

[!lowtech] A family of {FACTION} has turned up on foot, carrying what they could save. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} they need a few days, maybe longer, to work out where to go next, and they'll camp {PLACE} if the colony doesn't object.

settled.li: The family from {FACTION} put up a windbreak and laid out their beds around a fire {PLACE}. It almost looks like a home.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef}, from the family camped {PLACE}, came up to the colony this evening with a question {X_pronoun} has clearly been rehearsing. {X_nameDef} works hard, {X_pronoun} says, and would like to stay.

farewell.li: The family from {FACTION} packed up their camp {PLACE} and went on down the road. {X_nameDef} waved until the colony was out of sight.
The family from {FACTION} found somewhere to go, or decided to look for it. Their camp {PLACE} is empty now.

lines.li: Stay where I can see you.

texts.li: A band of prospectors of {FACTION} has come onto the colony's land with picks, pans and a lot of confidence. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} there's ore in this ground, and they mean to camp {PLACE} until they find it.

[lowtech] Prospectors of {FACTION} have arrived with mules' worth of tools on their own backs. {X_nameDef} says an old map brought them here. They will camp {PLACE} and dig, and they'll sell whatever they find.

[!lowtech] Prospectors of {FACTION} have turned up with sample bags and a battered ground scanner that {X_nameDef} swears still works. They plan to camp {PLACE} and dig test holes until they hit something.

settled.li: The prospectors from {FACTION} finished their camp {PLACE}, with a windbreak against the weather and a torch to dig by.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef} from the prospectors' camp is tired of digging holes for other people's fortunes, and asks whether the colony could use a steady pair of hands.

farewell.li: The prospectors from {FACTION} filled in their last holes, packed up their camp {PLACE} and moved on, still sure the big find is over the next hill.
The prospectors from {FACTION} broke camp {PLACE} and left, arguing about where to dig next.

lines.li: There's a seam here, I can feel it.

texts.li: Pilgrims of {FACTION} have stopped on the colony's land to rest. {X_nameDef}, who leads them, told {A_nameDef} their road is long and their feet are sore, and they'd like to camp {PLACE} for a few days before they go on.

A small band of pilgrims of {FACTION} is walking toward a holy place far from here. They've asked to rest {PLACE} for a few days, to pray and mend their sandals. {X_nameDef} promises they'll take very little.

settled.li: The pilgrims from {FACTION} made a simple camp {PLACE}, with a place set aside for prayer.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef}, one of the pilgrims camped {PLACE}, says the road has given {X_objective} what {X_pronoun} came for, and asks whether {X_pronoun} might stay with the colony instead of walking on.

farewell.li: The pilgrims from {FACTION} rested, prayed, and went on their way. {X_nameDef} said they'd remember the colony in their prayers.
The pilgrims from {FACTION} broke camp {PLACE} at dawn and walked on toward their holy place.

lines.li: Mind your feet, they're all you have.

texts.li: Traders of {FACTION} have decided the colony is worth more than a day's visit. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} they'll set up a stall {PLACE} and stay a few days, and anyone with silver is welcome.

[lowtech] A small band of traders of {FACTION} has stopped on the colony's land with packs full of goods. They mean to put up a stall {PLACE} and sell to the colony for a few days, the way market folk do.
[!lowtech] Traders of {FACTION} have arrived with packs, a folding table and a hand-painted sign. {X_nameDef} says they'll camp {PLACE} and keep the stall open for a few days.

settled.li: The traders from {FACTION} have their stall up {PLACE}, with a torch to see the goods by.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef}, who carries the traders' packs, has had enough of the road, and asks whether the colony would take on someone who can count and lift.

farewell.li: The traders from {FACTION} packed their stall and moved on to the next settlement.
Business was what it was. The traders from {FACTION} folded up their stall {PLACE} and left.

lines.li: Fair prices, best on the road!

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a traveling smith of {FACTION}, has come onto the colony's land with helpers and a cart of tools. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} they'll camp {PLACE} for a few days, sell what they've made, and mend what they can.

[medieval] A smith of {FACTION} has stopped near the colony with an anvil on a cart and apprentices to push it. {X_nameDef} means to camp {PLACE}, burn some charcoal and sell blades and mail to anyone who can pay.

settled.li: The smith from {FACTION} set up a work spot and a table of wares at the camp {PLACE}. The ringing of a hammer carries all the way to the colony.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef}, who has been working the smith's bellows, wants to stop moving, and asks whether the colony needs someone who knows metal.

farewell.li: The smith from {FACTION} loaded the cart and moved on, the anvil ringing faintly over every bump in the road.

texts.li: A hermit called {X_nameDef}, once of {FACTION}, has walked onto the colony's land and started pacing out a spot {PLACE}. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef}, in very few words, that {X_pronoun} means to build a hut and stay the season.
{X_nameDef}, a hermit who left {FACTION} years ago, has chosen a spot {PLACE} to build a hut for the season. {X_nameDef} asks nothing of the colony and seems to hope the colony will ask nothing back.

settled.li: {X_nameDef} finished a small hut {PLACE}, with a door, a roof and a fire outside it.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef}, the hermit camped {PLACE}, came to the colony's door this evening. After a long silence, {X_pronoun} asked whether there might be room for one more.

farewell.li: {X_nameDef} shut the door of the hut {PLACE} one last time and walked off without looking back. The hut is the colony's now, if it wants it.
